top_items.title: GTA 6 Gym Workouts Have A Useful Trick That Saves You A Lot Of Time
top_items.summary: You won't get muscles in real life without putting in some work, but fortunately, leveling up your pectorals in Grand Theft Auto 6 is much less strenuous. The only cardio you'll need to do is a series of finger movements on your controller, but admittedly, getting either of the game's protagonists into shape can be time-consuming. Fortunately, there's a trick that can help you cut workout times in half, which I wish I could apply to real life as well. Essentially, all you need to do in GTA 6 is make sure you're going to the gym as a couple. If you only focus on Jason or Lucia for a workout, then they'll gradually gain muscle and tone up on their own. But if you go as a pair, it doesn't matter who you work out with; both characters will gain and progress on their path toward becoming absolute units . That makes for a quick way to bulk up, though we still need to talk about Jason's gym etiquette . Pain and gains. This isn't the first time GTA has introduced gym gameplay mechanics to keep your protagonist in shape; back in GTA: San Andreas, players could frequent locations across the map and work on CJ's appearance. Not only could he increase his muscle mass and stamina by pumping iron, but CJ could also learn new fighting styles from trainers along the way. Working out in GTA 6 also has benefits, as lifting weights can improve overall health, while cardio activities like running and biking improve stamina. You can even track Jason and Lucia's workouts via a smartphone app, and there's an optimal time for them to train to maximize their efforts. You can do that either at a proper gym in the game world or, if you're on a budget, use the set of weights outside Jason's house. With GTA 6 out in the wild, players are quickly discovering just how much there is to do in Rockstar's massive open-world game. If you're one of them and looking for tips and tricks, check out GameSpot's GTA 6 guides hub for walkthroughs to help you out.

top_items.title: GTA 6 Has A Metacritic Score So High It’s Only Happened Once Before
top_items.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 has officially launched, and unsurprisingly, it's earning rave reviews. It's arriving hot on the heels of several critically acclaimed games this year, but does it have enough momentum to knock the current best-reviewed game of the year, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, off its throne? The answer is a resounding yes: not only is GTA 6 being reviewed higher than Nintendo's little hero in green, but it's also emerging as one of the highest-rated games of all time. When Ocarina of Time launched in early November, it quickly shot to the top of the Metacritic charts, earning a metascore of 96 from GameSpot's sister site. That score came from 128 reviews, and Metacritic rates it as "Universal Acclaim" on its scale. For GTA 6, the game is sitting on a review aggregate of 99 from 98 reviews at the time of writing, with just a single point keeping it away from a perfect score. One thing to note is that Ocarina of Time had more reviews than GTA 6, which affects the review weighting, but overall, both games drew from a broad pool of outlets worldwide. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ftI6gjFsPuw GTA 6 is only the second game to earn a metascore of 98, and hilariously, it's tied with the original Ocarina of Time from 1998. Historically, GTA games have always had some of the highest review aggregates, especially after the series moved to the third dimension. Starting with GTA 3, mainline entries have all earned metascores in the high 90s, with Grand Theft Auto 4 being the highest-reviewed game in the franchise until GTA 6 came along. Here's a closer look at those metascores over the years.: Grand Theft Auto — No metascore Grand Theft Auto 2 — 70 Grand Theft Auto 3 — 97 Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas — 95 Grand Theft Auto 4 — 98 Grand Theft Auto 5 — 97 Don't feel too bad for Ocarina of Time losing its crown, because the only thing better than critical success is commercial success. The remake has sold more than 5 million copies globally in its first four days, and those numbers will keep growing as we enter the festive season. Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick recently reacted to the game's release, saying it's "terrific" and that Nintendo has every right to be proud of it. "This game is the culmination of everything the developer has previously achieved in the open-world space that pushes the genre to heights that, in all likelihood, no other developer will be able to reach. GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I’d wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7," GameSpot editor-at-large Tamoor Hussain wrote in GameSpot's GTA 6 review . If you're planning to start playing it, you can also check out GameSpot's massive GTA 6 guides hub for all the tips and tricks you need to explore Vice City.

Developer Rockstar Games has revealed that it'll be evolving its subscription service to cover both GTA Online and GTA 6, and for $8 a month, players can unlock several in-game benefits, including store discounts, more public transit options, and better haggling power. If you've preordered GTA 6, you'll automatically get a month of GTA+ for free. One thing to note: the services below are only available while you're subscribed, so if your membership expires or you cancel, those perks will no longer be available. Here's a breakdown of what you'll get if you stay subscribed. Venturas Blvd Elegy supercar and garage Looks do matter in Vice City, and nothing looks better than a '90 Annis Venturas BLVD Elegy supercar when you hit the streets. This high-speed vehicle can be safely stored in a single-car garage in Crosstown, which also includes a weapon locker and the ability to fence stolen items directly. You'll gain access to it after you complete Chapter 3 in GTA 6. Transit Service Bonuses If you'd prefer to rely on public transit, you can grab an upgrade for these facilities. This includes Scooter Bros Premium, premium membership on the RydeMe rideshare app, free scooter, bike, and Seashark rentals, and free rides on Leonida public transportation. Store discounts Select businesses across the city will also offer you a 10% discount on their services. Weapons and clothes shops, hairdressers, tattooists, vehicle mod shops, and more are included. Increased sell value Selling an eligible vehicle will also net you an extra 10% in cash. Meanwhile, GTA Online players are also getting plenty of bang for their buck with GTA+ this month, as they can unlock a free car, in-game discounts, the Vinewood Car Club features, bonuses, and more. Are you planning to visit Vice City? Then check out GameSpot's comprehensive GTA 6 guides hub for all the tips, tricks, and walkthroughs to give you a leg up as you rise to the top of the crime food chain. From a list of GTA 6 cheat codes to a walkthrough on how to tempt fate by getting a six-star wanted level , there's plenty to dig into here. GTA 6 is currently earning rave reviews , and on GameSpot, it's the second game released this year to earn an extremely rare perfect score. "Rockstar's most ambitious game yet was worth the wait," GameSpot editor-at-large Tamoor Hussain wrote in GameSpot’s GTA 6 review .

items.title: Doctor whose evidence helped to convict Lucy Letby was barred from treating patients during trial
items.summary: Exclusive: Jury was never told that Prof Peter Hindmarsh was barred from practising over concerns for patients’ safety A senior doctor whose evidence helped to convict Lucy Letby and who was held up by prosecutors as a pre-eminent expert was barred from treating patients during the trial over fears he posed a risk to their safety. Prof Peter Hindmarsh, a specialist in hormones in children, was crucial to the crown’s argument that Letby had poisoned children by injecting insulin into fluid bags. But a Guardian investigation can reveal he was excluded from clinical practice in March 2023, five months before the end of the trial, by his employer, University College London hospitals trust (UCLH). Jurors were never told. Continue reading...

items.title: GTA 6 Has A Metacritic Score So High It’s Only Happened Once Before
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 has officially launched, and unsurprisingly, it's earning rave reviews. It's arriving hot on the heels of several critically acclaimed games this year, but does it have enough momentum to knock the current best-reviewed game of the year, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, off its throne? The answer is a resounding yes: not only is GTA 6 being reviewed higher than Nintendo's little hero in green, but it's also emerging as one of the highest-rated games of all time. When Ocarina of Time launched in early November, it quickly shot to the top of the Metacritic charts, earning a metascore of 96 from GameSpot's sister site. That score came from 128 reviews, and Metacritic rates it as "Universal Acclaim" on its scale. For GTA 6, the game is sitting on a review aggregate of 99 from 98 reviews at the time of writing, with just a single point keeping it away from a perfect score. One thing to note is that Ocarina of Time had more reviews than GTA 6, which affects the review weighting, but overall, both games drew from a broad pool of outlets worldwide. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ftI6gjFsPuw GTA 6 is only the second game to earn a metascore of 98, and hilariously, it's tied with the original Ocarina of Time from 1998. Historically, GTA games have always had some of the highest review aggregates, especially after the series moved to the third dimension. Starting with GTA 3, mainline entries have all earned metascores in the high 90s, with Grand Theft Auto 4 being the highest-reviewed game in the franchise until GTA 6 came along. Here's a closer look at those metascores over the years.: Grand Theft Auto — No metascore Grand Theft Auto 2 — 70 Grand Theft Auto 3 — 97 Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas — 95 Grand Theft Auto 4 — 98 Grand Theft Auto 5 — 97 Don't feel too bad for Ocarina of Time losing its crown, because the only thing better than critical success is commercial success. The remake has sold more than 5 million copies globally in its first four days, and those numbers will keep growing as we enter the festive season. Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick recently reacted to the game's release, saying it's "terrific" and that Nintendo has every right to be proud of it. "This game is the culmination of everything the developer has previously achieved in the open-world space that pushes the genre to heights that, in all likelihood, no other developer will be able to reach. GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I’d wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7," GameSpot editor-at-large Tamoor Hussain wrote in GameSpot's GTA 6 review . If you're planning to start playing it, you can also check out GameSpot's massive GTA 6 guides hub for all the tips and tricks you need to explore Vice City.

items.title: GTA 6 Has A Clever PS5 DualSense Trick For Keeping You Under The Speed Limit
items.summary: While the urge to be an absolute menace in Grand Theft Auto 6 is strong, nothing stops you from playing as a law-abiding citizen who sticks to the speed limit between missions. This option to avoid attracting local law enforcement's attention will probably be best experienced on PS5, thanks to one key advantage: the DualSense controller and its adaptive triggers. On PS5, GTA 6 players can keep their vehicle from going over the speed limit, as the adaptive triggers provide resistance when you get close to the legal limit. That doesn't mean that you can't break past that barrier, but the adaptive triggers will help you match traffic speed most of the time and stick to legal restrictions. That essentially makes it easier to control your vehicle and gives your index fingers a sense of how hard to press the triggers--useful when you're trying to avoid dinging your car by finding that sweet spot. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wmKu9Uow-os&t=2s This is just one of several vehicle-specific features in GTA 6, as the game borrows a few ideas from modern-day open-world games and puts its own spin on it. For example, you can summon your car via a smartphone app, which involves a Scooter Bros. employee appearing at your location, delivering your ride, and then disappearing into the sunset with the little two-wheeled ride they stashed in your trunk. Cars appear to be more important than ever in GTA 6, and stealing a fresh set of wheels is also something that has a little more friction to it, as you could boost a junker with an empty tank of fuel or an expensive sports car that has GPS tracking inside of it. items.title: GTA 6 Gym Workouts Have A Useful Trick That Saves You A Lot Of Time
items.summary: You won't get muscles in real life without putting in some work, but fortunately, leveling up your pectorals in Grand Theft Auto 6 is much less strenuous. The only cardio you'll need to do is a series of finger movements on your controller, but admittedly, getting either of the game's protagonists into shape can be time-consuming. Fortunately, there's a trick that can help you cut workout times in half, which I wish I could apply to real life as well. Essentially, all you need to do in GTA 6 is make sure you're going to the gym as a couple. If you only focus on Jason or Lucia for a workout, then they'll gradually gain muscle and tone up on their own. But if you go as a pair, it doesn't matter who you work out with; both characters will gain and progress on their path toward becoming absolute units . That makes for a quick way to bulk up, though we still need to talk about Jason's gym etiquette . Pain and gains. This isn't the first time GTA has introduced gym gameplay mechanics to keep your protagonist in shape; back in GTA: San Andreas, players could frequent locations across the map and work on CJ's appearance. Not only could he increase his muscle mass and stamina by pumping iron, but CJ could also learn new fighting styles from trainers along the way. Working out in GTA 6 also has benefits, as lifting weights can improve overall health, while cardio activities like running and biking improve stamina. You can even track Jason and Lucia's workouts via a smartphone app, and there's an optimal time for them to train to maximize their efforts. You can do that either at a proper gym in the game world or, if you're on a budget, use the set of weights outside Jason's house. With GTA 6 out in the wild, players are quickly discovering just how much there is to do in Rockstar's massive open-world game. If you're one of them and looking for tips and tricks, check out GameSpot's GTA 6 guides hub for walkthroughs to help you out.

items.title: Goal Zero’s Alta 50 cooler, Yeti 700 power station and Nomad 100 solar panel keep food cold
items.summary: Brian Riepe tested Goal Zero’s Yeti 700 power station, Alta 50 electric cooler and Nomad 100 solar panel for eight weeks and found that the system added a high degree of luxury to his camping. “I’m happy enough sleeping in a tent, I prefer to cook outside and I don’t mind ‘roughing it’ without a built-out Sprinter van,” he writes, “but adding solar electric power and getting rid of the melting ice and the soggy food in a standard cooler made every trip better. With a solar electric fridge, food stays dry and cold, and there’s no ice to buy or drain…. “Setup was about as easy as it gets. It took me fewer than 10 minutes to unbox everything, plug it in and have it running. Goal Zero makes larger and more powerful options for each component. For my purposes, I was happy with my choice to stay lighter and smaller.” The post Goal Zero’s Alta 50 cooler, Yeti 700 power station and Nomad 100 solar panel keep food cold appeared first on Alpinist .
